metadata.description: Spyder — HUD-style Jarvis UI skills for React and Blazor (.NET)

plugins.name: jarvis-ui-react
plugins.description: JARVIS UI React — HUD-style sci-fi React component library with 57+ components. Movies/SHIELD HUD canvas with drag-drop widgets (JHudCanvas, JDragWidget, JHudClock, JArcReactor, JHeatmap, JActivityFeed, JKPITicker) + full suite (JButton, JModal, JTable, JNodeGraph, JRadialMenu, JCommandPalette, JBootScreen...)

plugins.name: jarvis-ui-blazor
plugins.description: JARVIS UI Blazor — cinematic HUD-style Blazor (.NET/C#/Razor) component library with 57+ components (JButton, JModal, JTable, JLeafletMap, JGoogleMap, JNodeGraph, JRadialMenu...)

plugins.name: teamhub-team
plugins.description: TeamHub Team Protocol — Team Lead / Developer / Tester / Analyst / Project Planner skills for a multi-agent Claude Code team, backed by a self-hosted, project-aware TeamHub MCP server (SQLite-backed, no Jira required, shared-token auth, live member presence). Requires running the teamhub MCP server separately — see the plugin README. Supports an optional auto/manual mode with real mid-task interrupt from the Lead.

plugins.name: agent-memory
plugins.description: Agent Memory — creates and maintains a .claude/ folder at the project root: persistent, stack-agnostic AI memory with an INDEX, AGENT rules/state, per-session, per-task, and per-decision files, ARCHITECTURE, CODEBASE_MAP, a DECISIONS index, and optional CONTEXT/ files (including a per-controller API index). Activates ambiently — no slash command needed: auto-plans against existing memory before new work and auto-updates the relevant files as work happens. Progressive-disclosure design (slim SKILL.md + on-demand references/) keeps token use low. Works across C#, C++, Python, Go, React, Next.js, Blazor, Ruby, Java, Rust and more.

plugins.name: assistant
plugins.description: Assistant — a personal AI life companion (name/gender/tone chosen at onboarding, JARVIS-style) that manages PC control, Gmail, GitHub, calendar, daily planning, reminders, and family updates. Memory lives in a wiki-style ~/.assistant/ folder: one INDEX.md entry point linking to topic indexes (IDENTITY, FAMILY, PROJECTS, TASKS, DAILY, HEALTH, REMINDERS, KNOWLEDGE), each linking into its own subfolder of small per-item files — low context even after years of history. Ambient activation, no slash command — recognizes being addressed by its user-chosen name (e.g. 'Maya, check my email') even though that name isn't known until onboarding. Cross-skill aware: if a project already has its own memory skill (e.g. agent-memory), this skill stores only a pointer instead of duplicating detail.
